'''''Tillandsia xerographica''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Bromeliaceae|bromeliad]] family. It is native to southern [[Mexico]], [[El Salvador]], [[Guatemala]] and [[Honduras]].<ref name="Garcia">{{cite web |url=http://www.conabio.gob.mx/institucion/cooperacion_internacional/TallerNDF/Links-Documentos/WG-CS/WG2-Perennials/WG2-CS7%20Tilandsia/WG2-CS7-S.pdf |first=Mygdalia |last=García |author2=Hiram Ordóñez Chocano  |title=Case Study: ''Tillandsia xerographica'' |work=International Expert Workshop on CITES Non-Detriment Findings |access-date=2012-08-14}}</ref> The name is derived from the [[Greek language|Greek]] words ξηρός (''xeros''), meaning "dry", and γραφία (''graphia''), meaning "writing". It is included in [[Tillandsia subg. Tillandsia|''Tillandsia'' subg. ''Tillandsia'']].<ref>{{cite book |first=Paul T. |last=Isley |title=Tillandsia: the World's Most Unusual Air Plants |volume=1 |publisher=Botanical Press |page=187}}</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Tillandsia-xerographica.jpg|left|thumb|358x358px|''Tillandsia xerographica'']]
''Tillandsia  xerographica'' is a slow-growing, [[Xerophyte|xerophytic]] [[epiphyte]].<ref name="Garcia" /> The greenish silver leaves are wide at the base and taper to a point making an attractive, sculptural rosette, {{cvt|3|ft|cm|-1|order=flip}} or more in diameter and over {{cvt|3|ft|cm|-1|order=flip}} high in flower. The inflorescence, on a thick, green stem, {{cvt|6-15|in|mm|order=flip|round=5}} in height, is densely branched. The leaf bracts are rosy red; the floral bracts are chartreuse; and the petals of the tubular flowers are red to purple and are very long lasting (months).

== Habitat ==
[[File:Tillandsia xerographica (TS) 2-06882.jpg|thumb|left|''Tillandsia xerographica'' in its natural habitat in [[El Salvador]] near Los Cobanos beach]]
''Tillandsia  xerographica'' inhabits [[Tropical and subtropical dry broadleaf forests|dry forests]] and [[Deserts and xeric shrublands|thorn scrub]] at elevations of 140 to 600 m in southern [[Mexico]], [[Guatemala]] and [[El Salvador]]. Average temperatures in its habitat range from 22 °C to 28 °C, with relative humidity between 60% and 72% and annual precipitation between 550 and 800 mm.<ref name="Garcia"/> It grows epiphytically on the highest branches, where it receive intense lighting.
